newsitem.title: USA: Mattel to acquire Tyco Toys for $755 million in stock. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mattel to acquire Tyco Toys for $755 million in stock. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]

text.p: Mattel Inc., which failed to acquire rival Hasbro Inc. early this year, said Monday that it was acquiring Tyco Toys Inc. in a stock transaction valued at $755 million.
"The outstanding worldwide potential for Tyco's well-known brands will be fully realised through this merger with Mattel," Mattel Chairman John Amerman said in a statement.
Under the agreement, Tyco shareholders will recieve Mattel stock worth $12.50 for each Tyco share.
The announcement said that, based on Friday's closing stock prices, the deal represents a 78 percent premium for Tyco shareholders. Mattel closed Friday at $30.625 and Tyco at $7.
Mattel, the nation's biggest toymaker, said that, if the merger is completed in the first half of 1997 as expected, it will add to its earnings in the first year.
The boards of both companies already have approved the merger, the announcement said.
Mattel, based in El Segundo, Calif., had made an unsolicited $5.2 billion bid for Hasbro in January but withdrew the offer in February in face of fierce Hasbro opposition.
Mattel's products include Barbie and Cabbage Patch Kids dolls, Fisher-Price infant pre-school toys, Hot Wheels toy cars and several lines of Disney products.
Tyco, based on Mt. Laurel, N.J., is best known for its Matchbox miniature cars and radio-controlled vehicles.
